skill.name: email-assistant

content.value_statement: Email work often needs quick summaries, clear replies, and careful sending controls. This skill guides Claude to draft concise Gmail responses and wait for approval before sending.
actual_capabilities: Lists recent emails when Gmail MCP tools are available.
Reads full email content after the user selects a message.
Summarizes long emails into key points.
Drafts short replies in the same language as the original email.
Formats drafts with recipient, subject, attachment, and body sections.
Requires explicit user approval before reply_email or send_email is used.
limitations: Requires configured Gmail MCP tools for reading or sending messages.
Does not send messages without explicit confirmation from the user.
Does not verify attachment contents beyond the available tool context.
Account selection can be ambiguous when the user has multiple Gmail accounts.

use_cases.title: Reply to customer messages
use_cases.description: Draft short, professional replies that match the language and context of incoming customer emails.

use_cases.title: Process a busy inbox
use_cases.description: Review recent emails, read selected threads, and summarize the important points before taking action.

use_cases.title: Send approved updates
use_cases.description: Prepare new email messages with clear subjects and content, then request approval before sending.

prompt_templates.title: Check recent emails
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my recent emails and summarize the important ones.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a reply
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the email from [sender] about [topic] and draft a short reply in the same language.

prompt_templates.title: Search and respond
prompt_templates.prompt: Find emails about [project], summarize the latest thread, and draft a concise response for my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a new message
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a new email to [recipient] with subject [subject]. Include [key points] and ask me before sending.

output_examples.input: Draft a reply to Marie confirming that I attached the requested document.
output_examples.output:
To: Marie
Subject: RE: Requested document

Bonjour,

Veuillez trouver ci-joint le document demandé.

Cordialement,
[Name]

Ready to send?

output_examples.input: Summarize the latest email from the supplier and suggest a reply.
output: Summary: The supplier confirms delivery for Friday and asks for a billing address.
Suggested reply: Confirm Friday works and provide the correct billing address.
The draft should be reviewed before sending.

output_examples.input: Send a new email to Alex about the meeting notes.
output_examples.output: I need the recipient address, subject, and key points before drafting. I will show the draft and wait for approval before sending.

best_practices: Review every draft carefully before approving the send action.
Specify the intended Gmail account when more than one account is connected.
Provide the desired tone, recipient, and key points for new messages.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the assistant to send an email without reviewing the draft.
Do not rely on the skill for legal, medical, or financial advice in email content.
Do not include secrets or passwords in email drafts or prompts.

faq.question: Can this skill send emails automatically?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the assistant to ask for explicit approval before sending any email.

faq.question: Does it support languages other than English?
faq.answer: Yes. It tells the assistant to match the language of the original email.

faq.question: What tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects Gmail MCP tools such as list_emails, read_email, search_emails, reply_email, and send_email.

faq.question: Can it handle attachments?
faq.answer: It can include attachment information in drafts when the connected Gmail tools provide that context.

faq.question: Is it safe for multiple Gmail accounts?
faq.answer: It asks the user which account to use when the correct account is unclear.

faq.question: Can it summarize long emails?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow includes summarizing key points when an email is long.
